tasks.title: Polynomial string hash
tasks.statement: Write a function poly_hash(s, base, mod): the hash of a string by the scheme h = 0; for each character h = (h * base + ord(character)) % mod. The empty string gives 0.
tasks.hint: One loop over the characters; take the remainder at every step so the number stays small.

tasks.title: Hashes of all windows
tasks.statement: Write a function window_hashes(s, k, base, mod): the list of polynomial hashes (h = h * base + ord(character), modulo mod) of all substrings of length k, from left to right. If k is greater than the length of the string, return an empty list. Compute the hash of the next window from the previous one in O(1) (a rolling hash): the check feeds in 500,000 characters and a window of 1000.
tasks.hint: The window hash is a polynomial: subtract the contribution of the outgoing character ord(s[i-k]) * base**(k-1), multiply by base and add the code of the new one. Compute the power once: pow(base, k-1, mod).

tasks.title: Division or multiplication
tasks.statement: Write a function max_bucket(keys, m, method): distribute the integer keys over m slots and return the size of the fullest one. method = 'division' — the slot number is key % m; method = 'multiplication' — ((key * 2654435769) % 4294967296) * m // 4294967296 (the constant is 2³² / golden ratio).
tasks.hint: Create a list of counters of length m; for each key compute the slot number by the chosen method and add one. The answer is max(counters).

tasks.title: Hash table with chaining
tasks.statement: Implement the class ChainedHashMap(capacity=8, hash_fn=None) — a table with chaining. The buckets are a list of lists of [key, value] pairs; the bucket number is hash_fn(key) % capacity (hash by default). Methods: put(key, value) (a new key goes to the end of the chain, an existing one is updated), get(key, default=None), remove(key) → True/False, key in m, len(m), keys(), the capacity property and max_chain() — the length of the longest chain. Growth: after inserting a NEW key, if len(m) > 0.75 * capacity, double the number of buckets and insert all pairs again (going through the old buckets in order, chains left to right).
tasks.hint: Growth: collect all the pairs, create twice as many empty buckets and insert the pairs again (without checking for growth again), otherwise the order and size will differ from the reference.

tasks.title: Linear probing
tasks.statement: Implement the class LinearProbingMap(capacity=8, hash_fn=None) — open addressing with linear probing: slots start, start+1, start+2, … wrapping around, where start = hash_fn(key) % capacity. The slots are the list self.slots: None (empty), TOMB (tombstone) or a tuple (key, value). Fields: size — live keys, used — live keys plus tombstones, probes — a counter of inspected slots. Every slot inspection in get / put / remove increases probes by 1 (from the starting slot up to the found key or to the first empty slot, inclusive). get walks past tombstones and stops at None. put first makes sure the key is absent (reaches None), and inserts into the first tombstone encountered, or if there was none, into the empty slot (then used += 1); an existing key is updated. remove places a tombstone (size -= 1). Growth: after inserting a NEW key into an empty slot (not into a tombstone), if used * 2 > capacity, rebuild the table at twice the size: go through the old slots in increasing index order and insert the live pairs (tombstones are dropped; probes does not change during the rebuild).
tasks.hint: A single search method _find(key) that returns the index of the key, of the first tombstone and of the empty slot will avoid duplication in get/put/remove. Don’t forget to count probes on every slot inspection.

tasks.title: Quadratic probing
tasks.statement: Implement the class QuadraticProbingMap(capacity=8, hash_fn=None) — like LinearProbingMap, but at step i (i = 0, 1, 2, …) the slot (start + i·(i+1)//2) % capacity is checked — triangular offsets 0, 1, 3, 6, 10…; for a size equal to a power of two they visit every slot. The slots are the list self.slots: None (empty), TOMB (tombstone) or a tuple (key, value). Fields: size — live keys, used — live keys plus tombstones, probes — a counter of inspected slots. Every slot inspection in get / put / remove increases probes by 1 (from the starting slot up to the found key or to the first empty slot, inclusive). get walks past tombstones and stops at None. put first makes sure the key is absent (reaches None), and inserts into the first tombstone encountered, or if there was none, into the empty slot (then used += 1); an existing key is updated. remove places a tombstone (size -= 1). Growth: after inserting a NEW key into an empty slot, if used * 2 > capacity, rebuild the table at twice the size (old slots in increasing index order, tombstones dropped, probes unchanged).
tasks.hint: The same skeleton as linear probing; only the index formula at step i changes: (start + i * (i + 1) // 2) % capacity.

tasks.title: Double hashing
tasks.statement: Implement the class DoubleHashMap(capacity=11, hash_fn=None) of a fixed prime size: at step i (i = 0, 1, 2, …) the slot (h + i·step) % capacity is checked, where h = hash_fn(key), step = 1 + h % (capacity − 1) is the second hash. The slots are the list self.slots: None (empty), TOMB (tombstone) or a tuple (key, value). Fields: size — live keys, used — live keys plus tombstones, probes — a counter of inspected slots. Every slot inspection in get / put / remove increases probes by 1 (from the starting slot up to the found key or to the first empty slot, inclusive). get walks past tombstones and stops at None. put first makes sure the key is absent (reaches None), and inserts into the first tombstone encountered, or if there was none, into the empty slot (then used += 1); an existing key is updated. remove places a tombstone (size -= 1). There is no growth: if no free slot (empty or tombstone) was found and the key is absent, raise OverflowError.
tasks.hint: The step of the second function is nonzero and coprime with the prime size, so capacity probes visit all the slots.

tasks.title: Robin Hood hash table
tasks.statement: Implement the class RobinHoodMap(capacity=8, hash_fn=None) for integer keys: fixed size, linear probing from start = hash_fn(key) % capacity. A slot is None or a list [key, value, d], where d is the distance to the home slot. put: go through the slots with d = 0, 1, 2, …; an empty one — place the entry; the same key — update the value; if the owner of the slot has a SMALLER d than ours — swap places and continue inserting the evicted one (its d in the next slot is 1 greater). get: stop at an empty slot or when the owner’s d is smaller than ours (the key is absent). remove: after finding the key, shift the following slots back until an empty slot or a slot with d = 0 is met. Every slot inspection in put and get adds 1 to probes. A put of a new key into a full table raises OverflowError (the table is unchanged).
tasks.hint: In put, the evicted owner’s d refers to the slot it was thrown out of; in the next slot it will be at d + 1. In remove, after finding the key, pull the following slots back, decreasing their d by 1.

tasks.title: Cuckoo hashing
tasks.statement: Implement the class CuckooHash(capacity=8) for non-negative integer keys: two tables t1 and t2 (lists of length capacity of None or [key, value] pairs); h1(k) = k % capacity, h2(k) = (k // capacity) % capacity. put: if the key is already present — update it; otherwise place it in t1[h1], evicting the occupant to its t2[h2], the one evicted from there back to t1, and so on, at most 32 evictions; if that fails — double capacity and insert everything again (including the one left without a home). get(key, default=None) checks t1[h1], then t2[h2]; every slot check increases self.probes, so a lookup costs at most two probes. Also needed are remove(key) → True/False, key in m and len(m).
tasks.hint: The eviction loop: item, t1[i] = t1[i], item; if item became None — done; otherwise do the same with t2 by h2(item). After 32 rounds, double capacity and insert everything again, not forgetting item.

tasks.title: A set on your own table
tasks.statement: The hash table HashMap is already in the starter code (it comes from the previous exercises). Build the class HashSet on top of it: add(x), remove(x) → True/False, x in s, len(s), union(other), intersection(other), difference(other) (each returns a NEW HashSet) and to_sorted_list(). The built-in set, dict and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: A set is a table where the value does not matter: add stores the pair (x, True), and everything else is delegated to the table. Build new sets by iterating over keys().

tasks.title: Word frequencies
tasks.statement: Write a function word_frequencies(text): the frequency of each word of the text (words are separated by spaces and newlines, case matters) — a list of pairs (word, count), sorted by decreasing count and, on ties, by word. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: m.put(w, m.get(w, 0) + 1) is the whole point. Then sorted(m.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])).

tasks.title: Two numbers with a given sum (on your own table)
tasks.statement: Write a function two_sum(nums, target): a pair of indices (i, j), i < j, such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. If there are several pairs, take the one with the smallest j, and on ties the smallest i. If there is no pair — None. The check feeds in 200,000 numbers: nested loops will not make it in time. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: Go from left to right: has the needed “target − x” already been seen? Then the pair is found. Otherwise remember x → index (the first occurrence only).

tasks.title: First unique letter
tasks.statement: Write a function first_unique(s): the index of the first character that occurs in the string exactly once, or −1. The check feeds in 500,000 characters. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: Two passes: the first counts frequencies, the second returns the index of the first character with frequency 1.

tasks.title: Anagram groups
tasks.statement: Write a function group_anagrams(words): split the words into groups of anagrams. The result is a list of groups; inside a group the words are sorted, and the groups are sorted among themselves (as lists). The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: The group key is the sorted letters of the word: “eat” and “tea” give “aet”. The value is a list of words; a list can be stored in the table and appended to.

tasks.title: Subarrays with sum k
tasks.statement: Write a function count_subarrays(nums, k): how many non-empty contiguous subarrays have sum k (the numbers may be negative). The check feeds in 200,000 numbers. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: A prefix sum total; a suitable subarray ends here if the prefix sum total − k occurred earlier. The table stores how many times each prefix sum occurred (initially 0 occurred once).

tasks.title: Longest consecutive run
tasks.statement: Write a function longest_consecutive(nums): the length of the longest run of consecutive integers (for example, 100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2 → the run 1, 2, 3, 4 of length 4). The order in the array does not matter, duplicates are possible. Linear time is required: sorting will not do — the check feeds in 300,000 numbers, and each run must be built from its start exactly once. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: Put all the numbers into the table. Start a run only from a number that has no x − 1: then each number is visited at most twice.

tasks.title: Isomorphic strings
tasks.statement: Write a function is_isomorphic(s, t): True if the letters of string s can be replaced so that t results, with each letter always replaced by the same letter and different letters by different ones (one-to-one). The strings have the same length. Two tables are needed: s→t and t→s. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: Two tables are enough: what stands in t at the position of letter x (a) and what stands in s at the position of letter y (b); any contradiction means False.

tasks.title: LRU cache on your own table
tasks.statement: Implement the class LRUCache(capacity): get(key) → the value or −1 (an access makes the key the most recent); put(key, value) — add or update (also refreshes); when capacity is exceeded, the least recently used key is evicted. Both operations in O(1): the HashMap table stores nodes of the doubly linked list DNode, and the list orders the keys by recency (sentinels at the start and at the end will help). The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: get: find the node in the table, cut it out of the list, insert it after head. put: if the key exists — update and refresh; otherwise on overflow remove tail.prev (from both the list and the table), then insert the new node.

tasks.title: k most frequent
tasks.statement: Write a function top_k(nums, k): the k most frequent values of the array in order of decreasing frequency, and on equal frequencies by increasing value. It is guaranteed that k is not greater than the number of distinct values. Count the frequencies in the table. The check feeds in 300,000 numbers. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: The frequencies are in the table; then sort items() by (−frequency, value) and take the first k values.

tasks.title: Nearby duplicates
tasks.statement: Write a function contains_nearby_duplicate(nums, k): True if there are two different indices i and j with nums[i] == nums[j] and |i − j| ≤ k. The table stores the last index of each value. The check feeds in 400,000 numbers. The ready-made HashMap table is in the starter code — use only its put / get / remove / in / len / keys / items. Dict and set literals, dict(), set() and imports are forbidden.
tasks.hint: Walk through the array and remember the last index of each value. If you find a value seen no more than k steps back — the answer is True.
